source: The Westminster Shorter Catechism (1647), standard traditional text as published by the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (opc.org/sc.html)

items.label: Day 1
items.title: Made for God's Glory
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q1

Q. What is the chief end of man?

A. Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him forever.

Morning

1 Corinthians 10:31

Everything we do today, from breakfast to homework to chores, can be done for God's glory. That is not a heavy weight but a happy purpose: we were made to know God and delight in Him. In Jesus, the God we were made for has come near so that we can enjoy Him forever.

Father, You made us for Yourself. Let our eating, working, and playing today show that You are our greatest joy, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

Evening

Luke 10:38–42

Martha is busy and anxious; Mary sits at Jesus' feet, and He says she has chosen the good portion. We were made in the garden to walk with God, and the fall turned us into anxious workers. Jesus restores the first thing first.

Talk together

  • Younger: Where did Mary sit while Jesus was teaching?
  • Older: Why do you think Jesus called listening to Him "the good portion"?
  • Parents: Do I mostly treat God as a task to complete or as a Person to enjoy?

Who God is: A generous Lord who gives Himself as His people's portion, not a master who only wants our labour.

Who we are: Creatures made to enjoy God, who in our fallenness keep trying to earn what He freely gives.

Who Jesus is: The Lord of the covenant in person, sitting in a home in Bethany, inviting sinners to receive Him.

Closing prayer

Thank Jesus that He gives Himself to us as the good portion that can never be taken away.

items.label: Day 2
items.title: The Only Rule
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q2

Q. What rule hath God given to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him?

A. The Word of God, which is contained in the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, is the only rule to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him.

Morning

2 Timothy 3:16–17

God has not left us guessing about how to live. He has spoken in His Word, and it is enough. When we open the Bible together, we are hearing the voice of the God who loves us and shows us His Son.

Lord, thank You for speaking to us in the Scriptures. Give us ears to hear, hearts to trust, and hands to obey, for the sake of Christ, Your living Word. Amen.

Evening

Luke 24:13–27

Two downcast disciples walk to Emmaus, and the risen Jesus opens all the Scriptures, from Moses and the Prophets, to show them Himself. From creation to new creation, the Bible is one covenant story with one hero.

Talk together

  • Younger: Who was walking with the two disciples on the road?
  • Older: What does it mean that all the Scriptures are about Jesus?
  • Parents: Do I come to the Bible looking for rules alone, or looking for Christ?

Who God is: The God who speaks, keeps His word across the centuries, and patiently opens blind eyes.

Who we are: Slow of heart to believe, needing God's Word and Spirit, yet walked with and taught by our risen Lord.

Who Jesus is: The centre of all Scripture: the promised Seed, Prophet, Priest, and King, who had to suffer and then enter His glory.

Closing prayer

Ask the Lord to open our eyes, like the disciples on the road, to see Jesus in all of Scripture.

items.label: Day 3
items.title: Believe and Obey
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q3

Q. What do the Scriptures principally teach?

A. The Scriptures principally teach what man is to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man.

Morning

Deuteronomy 29:29

The Bible tells us two great things: who God is and how He wants us to live. Notice the order. We first learn what God has done for us, and then we learn how to walk with Him. Grace always comes before duty.

God of truth, teach us what to believe about You and how to walk with You. Let our obedience today be glad thanks for Your grace in Jesus. Amen.

Evening

Nehemiah 8:1–12

Returned from exile, God's people hear the Law read and explained, and they weep over their sin. They are told not to grieve, for the joy of the Lord is their strength. The covenant God restores His people around His Word.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did Ezra read to all the people?
  • Older: Why were the people told to rejoice instead of weep?
  • Parents: Does God's Word in our home lead us to joy in His mercy, or only to guilt?

Who God is: Holy in His law and abounding in mercy, bringing exiles home and turning mourning into feasting.

Who we are: Covenant people who have broken His law and deserved exile, gathered again by grace to hear and obey.

Who Jesus is: The One who kept the law for us and bore its curse, so that God's Word now ends for us in joy.

Closing prayer

Praise God that in Jesus His Word ends in joy, and the joy of the Lord is our strength.

items.label: Day 4
items.title: What Is God?
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q4

Q. What is God?

A. God is a spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth.

Morning

John 4:24

God is not like us, only bigger. He has no beginning, He never changes, and He is perfect in wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth. That might feel overwhelming, but it is good news: the God who loves us in Christ will never stop being who He is.

Holy God, You are greater than we can imagine and nearer than we deserve. Fill us with wonder at who You are, and rest in Your unchanging love in Jesus. Amen.

Evening

Isaiah 6:1–8

Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up, hears "Holy, holy, holy," and cries that he is lost. A coal from the altar touches his lips, his guilt is taken away, and he is sent. John 12:41 says Isaiah saw the glory of Christ.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did the angels call out about God?
  • Older: Why was Isaiah afraid when he saw God?
  • Parents: Have I grown too casual about God's holiness, or too afraid to draw near through Christ?

Who God is: Infinitely holy and majestic, yet merciful, providing the altar that cleanses sinners.

Who we are: Creatures of unclean lips who cannot stand before Him, but who can be cleansed, forgiven, and sent.

Who Jesus is: The glorious Lord on the throne who became the sacrifice on the altar, so the unclean could be made clean.

Closing prayer

Worship the holy God who cleanses us by the sacrifice of Jesus and sends us to serve Him.

items.label: Day 5
items.title: The Living and True God
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q5

Q. Are there more Gods than one?

A. There is but one only, the living and true God.

Morning

Deuteronomy 6:4–5

There is only one true God. Everything else people worship, whether money, fame, comfort, or screens, is a false god that cannot save. The living God gives life, hears prayer, and acts. He alone deserves our whole heart.

Lord our God, the Lord is one. Turn our hearts from every idol, and help us love You with all that we are, because You first loved us in Christ. Amen.

Evening

1 Kings 18:20–39

On Mount Carmel the prophets of Baal cry out all day to a god who never answers. Elijah prays once, and fire falls from heaven on the sacrifice. The people cry, "The Lord, he is God."

Talk together

  • Younger: What fell from heaven when Elijah prayed?
  • Older: What things do people today trust in like Baal?
  • Parents: What competes most for my heart's trust and affection right now?

Who God is: The one living and true God, who hears, answers, and will not share His glory with idols.

Who we are: Image-bearers who keep limping between two opinions, trading the living God for silent idols.

Who Jesus is: The true sacrifice on whom the fire of God's judgment fell, so that idolaters could be brought home.

Closing prayer

Confess our idols and thank the living God who answered with fire on Christ instead of us.

items.label: Day 6
items.title: One God in Three Persons
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q6

Q. How many persons are there in the Godhead?

A. There are three persons in the Godhead; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory.

Morning

2 Corinthians 13:14

God is one God in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. We cannot fully explain this, but we can worship. Before the world began, God was already a family of perfect love, and in Christ He brings us into that love.

Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one God, we praise You. Let the grace of Christ, the love of the Father, and the fellowship of the Spirit be with our family today. Amen.

Evening

Matthew 3:13–17

At the Jordan, Jesus is baptized; the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father says, "This is my beloved Son." The Spirit who hovered over the waters at creation now rests on the One who will make all things new.

Talk together

  • Younger: What came down from heaven like a dove?
  • Older: Where do you see the Father, the Son, and the Spirit in this story?
  • Parents: Do I live as one welcomed by the Father because of His Son?

Who God is: Father, Son, and Spirit, one God, eternally rich in love before the world began.

Who we are: Sinners who need cleansing, welcomed into the Father's family by union with His Son.

Who Jesus is: The beloved Son who stood in the sinners' line, so that the Father's delight in Him would cover us.

Closing prayer

Praise the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit for making us part of God's family through Jesus.

items.label: Day 7
items.title: God's Eternal Purpose
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q7

Q. What are the decrees of God?

A. The decrees of God are his eternal purpose, according to the counsel of his will, whereby, for his own glory, he hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.

Morning

Ephesians 1:11

Nothing surprises God. Before time began, He planned everything that happens, and He works all things for His glory and the good of His people. That does not make our choices meaningless; it means our lives are held in wise and loving hands.

Sovereign Lord, You work all things according to the counsel of Your will. When our day goes differently than we planned, help us trust Your good purpose in Christ. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 50:15–21

Joseph's brothers fear revenge, but Joseph says, "You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good." God kept His covenant promise to Abraham's family through their very sin, and saved many lives.

Talk together

  • Younger: Was Joseph angry with his brothers at the end?
  • Older: How did God use something evil for good in Joseph's life and at the cross?
  • Parents: Is there a hard thing in my life I need to trust to God's good purpose?

Who God is: Sovereign over all things, even evil, and always working toward His covenant purposes.

Who we are: Sinners whose evil choices are real, yet who cannot frustrate God's saving plan.

Who Jesus is: The greater Joseph, rejected by His brothers and handed over, yet through His suffering He saves many (Acts 2:23).

Closing prayer

Thank God that He works even evil for good, and that His greatest plan was the cross of Jesus.

items.label: Day 8
items.title: Creation and Providence
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q8

Q. How doth God execute his decrees?

A. God executeth his decrees in the works of creation and providence.

Morning

Psalm 135:6

God does not only make plans; He carries them out. He made the world, and He keeps running it, down to the wind, the waves, and the snow outside. Every moment of today is in His hands.

Lord of heaven and earth, You made all things and rule all things. Give us peace today, knowing You hold our family, our town, and our country in Your care through Christ. Amen.

Evening

Jonah 1:1–17

Jonah runs from God's call, but the Lord hurls a wind, guides the lots, and appoints a great fish. Every creature obeys God except His prophet. Creation itself serves the Lord's purpose of mercy to the nations.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did God send to swallow Jonah?
  • Older: List everything in this story that obeyed God. Who did not?
  • Parents: Where am I running from what God has clearly asked of me?

Who God is: Lord of wind, sea, and fish, ruling all creation and pursuing His runaway servants in mercy.

Who we are: Prone to run from God, yet unable to outrun His providence or His grace.

Who Jesus is: The greater Jonah, who went down into the deep for our sin, not His own, and rose again (Matthew 12:40).

Closing prayer

Praise God who rules wind and waves, and who sent Jesus into death to bring runaways home.

items.label: Day 9
items.title: God the Maker
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q9

Q. What is the work of creation?

A. The work of creation is God’s making all things of nothing, by the word of his power, in the space of six days, and all very good.

Morning

Hebrews 11:3

God made everything from nothing, simply by speaking. The stars, the mountains, the moose and the maple tree all exist because He said so. And He called it all very good. Creation shows us a God who is powerful, generous, and full of joy.

Creator God, everything we see today came from Your word. Open our eyes to Your glory in creation, and turn our wonder into praise through Jesus, by whom all things were made. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 1:1–25

In the beginning God speaks, and light, sky, land, plants, stars, and creatures appear, and He sees that it is good. This is the first page of the covenant story, and the new heavens and earth will be its last.

Talk together

  • Younger: What was the very first thing God made by speaking?
  • Older: What does creation teach us about what God is like?
  • Parents: When did I last stop to praise God for something He made?

Who God is: All-powerful, wise, and generous, making everything from nothing by His word and delighting in it.

Who we are: Creatures who owe our very existence to Him, placed in a good world to receive it with thanks.

Who Jesus is: The eternal Word through whom all things were made (John 1:3), who will one day make all things new.

Closing prayer

Thank God for His good creation and for Jesus, the Word through whom all things were made.

items.label: Day 10
items.title: Made in God's Image
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q10

Q. How did God create man?

A. God created man male and female, after his own image, in knowledge, righteousness and holiness, with dominion over the creatures.

Morning

Genesis 1:27

Every person you meet today is made in God's image, from a newborn to a grandparent, from a friend to someone hard to love. God made us male and female, to know Him, to be righteous and holy, and to care for His world. That gives every person deep worth.

Father, thank You for making us in Your image. Help us treat every person today with honour, and renew Your image in us through Christ, the true image of God. Amen.

Evening

Psalm 8:1–9

David looks at the night sky and marvels that God would crown man with glory and honour and give him dominion. Hebrews 2 says we do not yet see all things under man's feet, but we do see Jesus.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did David see when he looked up at night?
  • Older: How is Jesus the perfect example of what a human being should be?
  • Parents: Whom do I find it hardest to treat as an image-bearer of God?

Who God is: The majestic Creator whose name is excellent in all the earth, mindful of small creatures.

Who we are: Image-bearers crowned with honour, who lost our dominion in Adam's fall.

Who Jesus is: The true Man, crowned with glory because He suffered death for us, who restores God's image in His people.

Closing prayer

Praise God for crowning us with honour and for Jesus, the true Man, who restores His image in us.

items.label: Day 11
items.title: God's Providence
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q11

Q. What are God’s works of providence?

A. God’s works of providence are his most holy, wise and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures, and all their actions.

Morning

Matthew 10:29–31

Not one sparrow falls to the ground apart from our Father. God preserves and governs every creature and every action. Nothing in our day is random. Our Father, who gave His Son for us, is caring for us in the details.

Heavenly Father, You care for sparrows and count the hairs on our heads. Calm our worries today, and help us trust Your wise and loving hand, through Jesus Christ. Amen.

Evening

Esther 4:1–17

A decree threatens to destroy the Jews in Persia, and Esther risks her life to plead for her people: "If I perish, I perish." God's name never appears in the book, yet He keeps His covenant people through it all.

Talk together

  • Younger: Who did Esther go to see, even though she was afraid?
  • Older: How do we see God working in Esther's story when His name is not mentioned?
  • Parents: Where might God have placed me "for such a time as this"?

Who God is: Hidden but never absent, ruling kings and calendars to preserve His people.

Who we are: A vulnerable covenant family, often afraid, placed by God for such a time as this.

Who Jesus is: The greater Mediator, who did not only risk His life before the King but laid it down to save His people.

Closing prayer

Thank God for His hidden but faithful providence, and for Jesus, who gave His life to save His people.

items.label: Day 12
items.title: The Covenant of Life
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q12

Q. What special act of providence did God exercise toward man in the estate wherein he was created?

A. When God had created man, he entered into a covenant of life with him, upon condition of perfect obedience; forbidding him to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.

Morning

Hosea 6:7

In the garden, God made a covenant with Adam: obey and live, disobey and die. God was generous, giving every tree but one. Adam failed, but God would send a second Adam to keep the covenant for us.

Gracious God, You have always been generous to us. Where we have failed to obey, thank You for Jesus, who obeyed perfectly in our place. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 2:8–17

God plants a garden full of good trees and freely gives every one but one: eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil and you will die. This covenant of life is the backdrop for the whole Bible.

Talk together

  • Younger: How many trees could Adam eat from? How many were forbidden?
  • Older: How was God generous even when He gave Adam a rule?
  • Parents: Do I see God's commands as stingy, or as the boundaries of a generous Father?

Who God is: Generous and good, giving freely and setting wise limits as a loving Lord.

Who we are: Creatures made upright and blessed, placed under God's covenant and called to trust and obey.

Who Jesus is: The last Adam, who kept every word of the covenant where Adam failed, and won life for His people.

Closing prayer

Thank Jesus, the last Adam, for keeping the covenant perfectly where we failed.

items.label: Day 13
items.title: The Fall
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q13

Q. Did our first parents continue in the estate wherein they were created?

A. Our first parents, being left to the freedom of their own will, fell from the estate wherein they were created, by sinning against God.

Morning

Ecclesiastes 7:29

God made our first parents upright, but they chose to sin. They were not forced; they listened to a lie and turned from God. We still do the same thing. But God did not leave them in their hiding place, and He does not leave us there either.

Lord, we confess that like our first parents we listen to lies and turn from You. Seek us out, cover our shame, and keep us near to Christ. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 3:1–13

The serpent asks, "Did God actually say?" Eve and Adam eat, see their shame, and hide. Then God comes walking in the garden, calling, "Where are you?" Here the fall begins, but so does God's pursuit.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did Adam and Eve do when they heard God coming?
  • Older: What lie did the serpent want Eve to believe about God?
  • Parents: When I sin, do I hide and blame, or run to God?

Who God is: Truthful and holy, and yet the seeking God who comes to sinners first.

Who we are: Image-bearers who doubted God's goodness, fell, and now hide and blame.

Who Jesus is: The Lord who came all the way into our world to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:10).

Closing prayer

Thank God that He comes looking for sinners, and that Jesus came to seek and save the lost.

items.label: Day 14
items.title: What Is Sin?
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q14

Q. What is sin?

A. Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, the law of God.

Morning

1 John 3:4

Sin is not only doing bad things. It is any way we fall short of God's law, in what we do, say, think, or fail to do. That shows us how much we need a Saviour. And it shows how great Christ's forgiveness is.

Holy Father, we confess our sins of doing and of not doing. Forgive us for Jesus' sake, and make us quick to repent and quick to believe Your mercy. Amen.

Evening

2 Samuel 12:1–13

Nathan tells David of a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb, then says, "You are the man!" David confesses, "I have sinned against the Lord," and Nathan answers that the Lord has put away his sin.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did the rich man in Nathan's story take?
  • Older: Why do you think Nathan told David a story instead of accusing him right away?
  • Parents: Is there a sin I keep excusing instead of naming before God?

Who God is: Holy and just, seeing every sin, and also merciful, faithful to His covenant with David.

Who we are: Sinners quick to judge others and blind to ourselves, needing God's Word to expose and heal us.

Who Jesus is: The greater Son of David, on whom the Lord laid the sin He put away from us.

Closing prayer

Confess our sin honestly, and thank God that He has put it away through Jesus, the Son of David.

items.label: Day 15
items.title: The Forbidden Fruit
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q15

Q. What was the sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created?

A. The sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created was their eating the forbidden fruit.

Morning

James 1:14–15

The first sin looked small: eating a piece of fruit. But it was really a refusal to trust God's word. Temptations often look small and pleasant. Jesus faced the tempter too, and He won where Adam lost.

Lord Jesus, You were tempted in every way and did not sin. When we are tempted today, help us remember Your word and lean on Your strength. Amen.

Evening

Matthew 4:1–11

Adam fell in a garden full of food; Jesus stands firm in a wilderness after forty days of hunger. Each time He answers the devil, "It is written." Where the first Adam doubted, the last Adam trusted.

Talk together

  • Younger: How did Jesus answer the devil each time?
  • Older: How is Jesus' temptation different from Adam's?
  • Parents: What temptation is hardest for me, and what Scripture could I hold onto?

Who God is: A faithful Father whose every word is true and enough to live by.

Who we are: Weak and easily tempted, as Adam's children, needing a champion and His Spirit's strength.

Who Jesus is: The obedient Son and last Adam, whose victory over temptation is counted to us.

Closing prayer

Praise Jesus for winning where Adam lost, and ask for His strength in temptation.

items.label: Day 16
items.title: Fallen in Adam
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q16

Q. Did all mankind fall in Adam’s first transgression?

A. The covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself, but for his posterity; all mankind, descending from him by ordinary generation, sinned in him, and fell with him, in his first transgression.

Morning

1 Corinthians 15:21–22

Adam did not sin only for himself. He stood as the head of all humanity, so when he fell, we fell with him. That can sound unfair, until we see the good news: God also gave a second Head, Jesus, and all who are in Him are made alive.

Father, we were lost in Adam, but You have given us life in Christ. Thank You for counting His obedience for us. Keep us in Him today. Amen.

Evening

Romans 5:12–21

Paul explains that sin and death came through one man, Adam, and righteousness and life come through one man, Jesus. Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more.

Talk together

  • Younger: Through whom did sin come into the world? Through whom does grace come?
  • Older: Why is it good news that we can have Jesus as our representative?
  • Parents: Do I believe that grace really abounds more than my sin?

Who God is: Just in judging sin, and lavish in grace that overflows beyond our sin.

Who we are: Fallen in Adam our covenant head, condemned with him, yet invited to be found in Christ.

Who Jesus is: The second Head, whose obedience makes many righteous and whose grace reigns to eternal life.

Closing prayer

Thank God that where sin increased, grace abounded all the more through Jesus Christ.

items.label: Day 17
items.title: Sin and Misery
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q17

Q. Into what estate did the fall bring mankind?

A. The fall brought mankind into an estate of sin and misery.

Morning

Romans 3:23

The fall brought two things: sin, which is our guilt and corruption, and misery, which is the brokenness and sorrow sin brings. We see both in the world and in our own hearts. But God does not leave sinners alone in their misery.

Merciful God, we see the sin and sorrow in our world and in ourselves. Do not leave us there. Draw us to Jesus, who carried our sin and sorrows. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 4:1–16

One generation after the fall, Cain envies and murders his brother Abel. Abel's blood cries out from the ground, yet God still marks Cain for protection. Sin has spread from a garden to a field to every human heart.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did Cain do to his brother Abel?
  • Older: What does Hebrews mean that Jesus' blood speaks a better word than Abel's?
  • Parents: Where is anger or envy crouching at the door of my heart?

Who God is: Just, hearing the cry of innocent blood, and patient, restraining evil and showing mercy.

Who we are: Fallen people whose sin crouches at the door and spreads misery to those we should love most.

Who Jesus is: The One whose sprinkled blood speaks a better word than Abel's: not vengeance, but pardon (Hebrews 12:24).

Closing prayer

Thank Jesus that His blood speaks a better word of mercy over sinners like us.

items.label: Day 18
items.title: Original Sin
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q18

Q. Wherein consists the sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell?

A. The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell consists in the guilt of Adam’s first sin, the want of original righteousness, and the corruption of his whole nature, which is commonly called original sin; together with all actual transgressions which proceed from it.

Morning

Ephesians 2:1–3

We are not sinners because we sin; we sin because we are sinners. From Adam we inherit guilt and a corrupted nature, and out of that come our daily wrong choices. That is why we need more than better habits. We need new hearts.

Lord, we need more than a fresh start; we need new hearts. Wash us, renew us, and let Christ's righteousness be our covering. Amen.

Evening

Psalm 51:1–12

After his sin, David confesses he was sinful from birth. He asks not for self-improvement but for a new heart: "Create in me a clean heart, O God," appealing to God's steadfast love.

Talk together

  • Younger: What colour does David ask God to make his heart, like fresh snow?
  • Older: Why does David ask for a new heart and not just to try harder?
  • Parents: Do I lean on God's mercy, or on my own efforts to be better?

Who God is: Rich in steadfast love and abundant mercy, able to create clean hearts.

Who we are: Sinners from the root, who need not a fresh coat of paint but new hearts.

Who Jesus is: The One whose blood washes us whiter than snow and whose Spirit gives the new heart God promised.

Closing prayer

Ask God to create clean hearts in each of us through the blood of Jesus.

items.label: Day 19
items.title: The Misery of the Fall
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q19

Q. What is the misery of that estate whereinto man fell?

A. All mankind by their fall lost communion with God, are under his wrath and curse, and so made liable to all the miseries in this life, to death itself, and to the pains of hell forever.

Morning

Galatians 3:13

Sin broke our friendship with God and brought His curse and every kind of sorrow, even death. This is serious, and we should not pretend otherwise. But the gospel tells us that Christ became a curse for us, so that the curse would be lifted from all who trust Him.

Lord Jesus, You bore the curse we deserved. When we feel the sorrows of this broken world, give us hope in Your cross and in the day You will make all things new. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 3:14–24

God pronounces the curse, and Adam and Eve are driven from Eden. Yet God promises that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head, and He clothes them Himself. Hope is spoken in the very hour of judgment.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did God make for Adam and Eve to wear?
  • Older: Where is the promise of a Saviour in this sad chapter?
  • Parents: How do I respond to the brokenness I see: with despair or with hope in Christ?

Who God is: Just in judgment and merciful in promise, keeping His word to both.

Who we are: Exiles from the garden, under the curse, unable to return on our own.

Who Jesus is: The promised Offspring who crushed the serpent, became a curse for us, and opens the way to the tree of life.

Closing prayer

Thank God that even in judgment He promised Jesus, who crushed the serpent and bore our curse.

items.label: Day 20
items.title: The Covenant of Grace
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q20

Q. Did God leave all mankind to perish in the estate of sin and misery?

A. God having, out of his mere good pleasure, from all eternity, elected some to everlasting life, did enter into a covenant of grace, to deliver them out of the estate of sin and misery, and to bring them into an estate of salvation by a redeemer.

Morning

Ephesians 1:4–5

God did not leave all mankind to perish. Out of His own good pleasure, before the world began, He chose a people to save and made a covenant of grace to rescue them through a Redeemer. Our salvation starts with God's love, not our goodness.

Father, before the world began You set Your love on Your people. Thank You for the covenant of grace in Jesus. Keep our family in it, and help us rest in Your choosing love. Amen.

Evening

Genesis 15:1–21

God promises Abram offspring like the stars, and Abram believes. Then a smoking fire pot and flaming torch pass alone between the pieces, as God binds Himself by covenant to keep His promise.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did God tell Abram to count in the night sky?
  • Older: Why is it important that only God passed between the pieces?
  • Parents: Do I rest in God's promise, or act as if it depends on me?

Who God is: Faithful and gracious, binding Himself by oath to save a people who cannot save themselves.

Who we are: Children of Abraham by faith, justified by believing God's promise, not by our own work.

Who Jesus is: The promised Seed, in whom God bore the covenant's cost Himself at the cross.

Closing prayer

Praise God, who bound Himself to save us and kept His covenant at the cross.

items.label: Day 21
items.title: The Only Redeemer
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q21

Q. Who is the redeemer of God’s elect?

A. The only redeemer of God’s elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so was, and continueth to be, God and man in two distinct natures, and one person, forever.

Morning

1 Timothy 2:5

There is only one Redeemer: the Lord Jesus Christ. He is the eternal Son of God who became man, and He is still God and man, forever. No one else can stand between us and God. And no one else needs to.

Lord Jesus, You are our only Redeemer, truly God and truly man. We trust in You alone today, and we praise You for coming to us. Amen.

Evening

John 1:1–14

The Word who was with God and was God, through whom all things were made, became flesh and dwelt among us. To all who receive Him, He gives the right to become children of God.

Talk together

  • Younger: What does John call Jesus at the start of his Gospel?
  • Older: Why did our Redeemer need to be both God and man?
  • Parents: Am I trusting Christ alone, or adding something of my own?

Who God is: Eternal, glorious, and full of grace and truth, coming near to dwell with His people.

Who we are: Darkened creatures who did not receive Him, now made children of God by new birth.

Who Jesus is: The eternal Son made flesh, truly God and truly man, the only Redeemer and true tabernacle.

Closing prayer

Worship Jesus, the Word made flesh, our only Redeemer, who gives us the right to be God's children.

items.label: Day 22
items.title: The Son Became Man
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q22

Q. How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?

A. Christ, the Son of God, became man, by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary, and born of her, yet without sin.

Morning

Hebrews 2:14, 17

Jesus did not just look human. He took a real body and a real human soul. He was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary, yet without sin. He knows what it is to be tired, hungry, and sad, and so He is a merciful and faithful Saviour.

Lord Jesus, thank You for taking our nature to save us. When we are weak or weary today, remind us that You understand and that You are near. Amen.

Evening

Luke 1:26–38

Gabriel tells Mary she will bear a Son, the Son of the Most High, whose kingdom will have no end. The Holy Spirit will overshadow her, for nothing is impossible with God. Mary answers in humble faith.

Talk together

  • Younger: What name did the angel tell Mary to give her baby?
  • Older: Why does it matter that Jesus was born without sin?
  • Parents: Do I respond to God's word with Mary's humble trust?

Who God is: Faithful to His promise to David and mighty to do the impossible.

Who we are: Humble servants called to receive God's word with trusting obedience.

Who Jesus is: The eternal Son who took a true body and soul, born without sin, the King on David's throne forever.

Closing prayer

Thank God for sending His Son to be born for us, truly God and truly man.

items.label: Day 23
items.title: Prophet, Priest, and King
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q23

Q. What offices doth Christ execute as our redeemer?

A. Christ, as our redeemer, executeth the offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in his estate of humiliation and exaltation.

Morning

Hebrews 1:1–3

Christ carries three offices for us. As Prophet He tells us the truth about God. As Priest He offers Himself and prays for us. As King He rules and protects us. Whatever we need, He is enough.

Lord Jesus, our Prophet, Priest, and King, teach us, cleanse us, and rule over us today. We gladly belong to You. Amen.

Evening

Matthew 2:1–12

Wise men from the east follow a star to Bethlehem and worship the child King with gold, frankincense, and myrrh, while King Herod is troubled. The promise to bless all nations through Abraham is coming true.

Talk together

  • Younger: What gifts did the wise men bring to Jesus?
  • Older: Why was Herod troubled while the wise men were glad?
  • Parents: Which of Christ's offices do I most need to remember this week?

Who God is: The God of all nations, guiding seekers to His Son and overruling proud kings.

Who we are: Gentiles once far off, now invited to bow and worship alongside God's covenant people.

Who Jesus is: The true King, the Shepherd of Israel from Bethlehem, worthy of worship from every nation.

Closing prayer

Worship Jesus as our Prophet, Priest, and King, and ask Him to reign in our home.

items.label: Day 24
items.title: Christ Our Prophet
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q24

Q. How doth Christ execute the office of a prophet?

A. Christ executeth the office of a prophet, in revealing to us, by his word and Spirit, the will of God for our salvation.

Morning

Deuteronomy 18:15

Moses promised that God would raise up a Prophet like him, and the people must listen to Him. Jesus is that Prophet. By His Word and Spirit, He shows us God's will for our salvation. When we read the Bible, we are sitting under His teaching.

Lord Jesus, You are the Prophet God promised. Speak to us by Your Word and Spirit today, and give us listening hearts. Amen.

Evening

Luke 9:28–36

On the mountain Jesus' face shines and His clothes become dazzling white. Moses and Elijah speak with Him, and the Father says, "This is my Son, my Chosen One; listen to him!" Then Jesus is found alone.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did Jesus' clothes look like on the mountain?
  • Older: What did the Father tell the disciples to do?
  • Parents: How well am I listening to Jesus in His Word each day?

Who God is: The God who speaks and wants His children to hear and heed His Son.

Who we are: Disciples prone to confusion and fear, needing to stop talking and listen.

Who Jesus is: The Prophet like Moses, greater than Moses, God's final word to whom the Law and Prophets point.

Closing prayer

Ask the Father to help our whole family listen to His Son, our Prophet.

items.label: Day 25
items.title: Christ Our Priest
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q25

Q. How doth Christ execute the office of a priest?

A. Christ executeth the office of a priest, in his once offering up of himself a sacrifice to satisfy divine justice, and reconcile us to God; and in making continual intercession for us.

Morning

Hebrews 7:25

A priest stands between God and sinners. Jesus offered Himself once as the perfect sacrifice to satisfy God's justice and bring us back to God. And right now He is still praying for us. We are never forgotten.

Great High Priest, thank You for offering Yourself once for all, and for praying for us now. Let us draw near to the Father with confidence today. Amen.

Evening

Leviticus 16:15–22

On the Day of Atonement the high priest offers blood in the Most Holy Place, then confesses Israel's sins over a live goat and sends it into the wilderness. One goat dies; the other carries sin away.

Talk together

  • Younger: Where did the second goat go, carrying the sins?
  • Older: How does Jesus fulfill both goats in this ceremony?
  • Parents: Am I living as someone whose sins have truly been carried away?

Who God is: Holy, unable to overlook sin, yet providing the way of atonement Himself.

Who we are: A covenant people stained by sin, needing both a sacrifice and a sending-away of guilt.

Who Jesus is: Our great High Priest, who is both sacrifice and sin-bearer, and who ever lives to intercede for us.

Closing prayer

Thank Jesus, our High Priest, who died for our sins and carried them away forever.

items.label: Day 26
items.title: Christ Our King
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q26

Q. How doth Christ execute the office of a king?

A. Christ executeth the office of a king, in subduing us to himself, in ruling and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all his and our enemies.

Morning

1 Corinthians 15:25

Jesus is King. He brings us under His loving rule, guards and guides us, and defeats every enemy, including sin, Satan, and death. His rule is not harsh. It is the safest place to live.

King Jesus, rule over our hearts and our home today. Defend us from every enemy, and give us joy in following You. Amen.

Evening

1 Samuel 17:32–50

Israel's army trembles before Goliath. Young David, the anointed future king, goes out in the Lord's name and fells the giant with a single stone. The whole army shares in a victory they did not fight.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did David use to defeat Goliath?
  • Older: Why is it better to see Jesus, not ourselves, as the David in this story?
  • Parents: What giant am I trying to fight on my own instead of trusting my King?

Who God is: The Lord who saves, not by sword and spear, but by His own power through His anointed.

Who we are: Not David but the frightened soldiers, unable to defeat our giants of sin and death.

Who Jesus is: The greater Son of David, who fought our enemies alone and won the victory for His people.

Closing prayer

Praise King Jesus, who fought our enemies alone and won the victory for His people.

items.label: Day 27
items.title: Christ's Humiliation
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q27

Q. Wherein did Christ’s humiliation consist?

A. Christ’s humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low condition, made under the law, undergoing the miseries of this life, the wrath of God, and the cursed death of the cross; in being buried, and continuing under the power of death for a time.

Morning

Philippians 2:6–8

The Son of God was born in a low condition, lived under the law, suffered in this life, bore God's wrath, died on a cross, and was buried. He went all the way down for us. There is no depth of sorrow where He has not been.

Lord Jesus, You humbled Yourself to the point of death on a cross. Give us Your humble mind today, and fill us with thankfulness for Your love. Amen.

Evening

Luke 23:33–49

Jesus is crucified between two criminals. He prays for His enemies, promises a dying thief paradise, darkness covers the land, and the temple curtain tears. He commits His spirit to the Father.

Talk together

  • Younger: What did Jesus promise the thief on the cross?
  • Older: Why was the temple curtain torn when Jesus died?
  • Parents: Where do I need Christ's humble mind in how I treat my family?

Who God is: Just in punishing sin and astonishingly merciful in providing the Substitute.

Who we are: Guilty like the thieves, deserving death, saved only by grace like the one who asked to be remembered.

Who Jesus is: The suffering Servant of Isaiah 53, bearing the curse of the cross to open the way to God.

Closing prayer

Thank Jesus for humbling Himself to the cross and opening the way to God for us.

items.label: Day 28
items.title: Christ's Exaltation
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q28

Q. Wherein consisteth Christ’s exaltation?

A. Christ’s exaltation consisteth in his rising again from the dead on the third day, in ascending up into heaven, in sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and in coming to judge the world at the last day.

Morning

Philippians 2:9–11

The story did not end at the grave. Jesus rose on the third day, ascended to heaven, sits at the Father's right hand, and will come again to judge the world. Every knee will bow to Him. Our King is alive and reigning now.

Risen and reigning Lord, we confess that You are Lord, to the glory of the Father. Give us hope and courage today as we wait for Your return. Amen.

Evening

Acts 1:6–11

Forty days after His resurrection, Jesus promises the Spirit, sends His disciples as witnesses to the end of the earth, and ascends. Angels say this same Jesus will come again in the same way.

Talk together

  • Younger: Where did Jesus go when the cloud took Him?
  • Older: What did the angels promise about Jesus coming back?
  • Parents: Am I living as a witness to a risen, reigning King?

Who God is: The God who finishes what He starts and is gathering a people from every nation.

Who we are: Witnesses sent by the King, living between His ascension and His return.

Who Jesus is: The risen, ascended King at the Father's right hand, who will return to judge and make all things new.

Closing prayer

Praise the risen and ascended Jesus, and ask Him to make us faithful witnesses until He comes.

items.label: Day 29
items.title: Redemption Applied
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q29

Q. How are we made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ?

A. We are made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.

Morning

Titus 3:5–6

Christ purchased our redemption on the cross, and the Holy Spirit applies it to us. What Jesus did long ago becomes ours today because the Spirit makes it ours. We cannot save ourselves, but the Spirit is mighty to save.

Holy Spirit, apply the work of Christ to each one in our home. Wash us, renew us, and make Jesus real to our hearts today. Amen.

Evening

Acts 2:36–41

Peter proclaims that God has made the crucified Jesus both Lord and Christ. The crowd is cut to the heart, and Peter calls them to repent and be baptized, for the promise is for them and their children.

Talk together

  • Younger: How many people believed on that day?
  • Older: Who did Peter say the promise was for?
  • Parents: Am I praying for the Spirit to apply Christ's work to my children's hearts?

Who God is: Faithful to His covenant promise across generations, pouring out His Spirit.

Who we are: Sinners cut to the heart, needing repentance, and families included in God's covenant promise.

Who Jesus is: The exalted Lord and Christ, who pours out the Spirit to apply the redemption He purchased.

Closing prayer

Thank God that His promise is for us and for our children, and ask the Spirit to work in each of us.

items.label: Day 30
items.title: United to Christ by Faith
items.html:
Westminster Shorter Catechism Q30

Q. How doth the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?

A. The Spirit applieth to us the redemption purchased by Christ, by working faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual calling.

Morning

Galatians 2:20

The Spirit gives us faith, and by faith we are joined to Jesus. We belong to Him and He lives in us. Faith is not something we produce; it is the Spirit's gift that unites us to all that Christ is.

Lord, we believe; help our unbelief. Thank You for the gift of faith and for joining us to Jesus. Let His life be seen in us today. Amen.

Evening

Ezekiel 37:1–14

In a valley of dry bones, Ezekiel preaches, the bones rattle together, and when God's breath enters them they stand up, a great army. God promises to put His Spirit in His people so they live.

Talk together

  • Younger: What happened to the dry bones when God's breath came into them?
  • Older: How is this story a picture of how God saves us?
  • Parents: Do I believe the Spirit can bring life where things seem dead?

Who God is: The life-giving God who raises the dead and keeps His covenant promises.

Who we are: Spiritually dead in sin, unable to raise ourselves, but made alive by His Word and Spirit.

Who Jesus is: The risen Lord whose Spirit gives us faith and joins us to His resurrection life.

Closing prayer

Praise the Spirit who gives life to dry bones and unites us by faith to the risen Jesus.
